context:
Patient: 45F teacher, ECOG 0, with a painless right neck node; no B symptoms, normal LDH; PET-CT shows FDG-avid right cervical level II-III nodes only (largest 3.1 cm), no extranodal or marrow uptake. Excisional biopsy: DLBCL NOS, GCB by Hans, MYC 15%, BCL2 30%, FISH negative for MYC/BCL2/BCL6; premenopausal on a combined ethinyl estradiol pill despite migraine with aura, no pregnancy test on file, and wants to avoid neck radiation.
What this case tests: A single contiguous neck region with no B symptoms and a 3.1 cm node is non-bulky stage IA, not advanced disease. | MYC 15% / BCL2 30% and negative FISH mean neither double-expressor nor double-hit, so no intensified regimen. | IPI 0, age under 60, non-bulky: 4 R-CHOP + 2 rituximab without radiotherapy (FLYER) is preferred; 6 cycles or Pola-R-CHP is overtreatment. | The combined estrogen pill must be stopped (migraine with aura = stroke risk, plus chemo-related VTE) and replaced with non-estrogen contraception. | No pregnancy test is documented in this premenopausal woman, so one is required before cycle 1.

answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL-NOS), de novo, germinal-center B-cell (GCB) subtype, involving right cervical lymph nodes (level IIA, largest 3.1 cm, and level III). There is no extranodal, splenic, hepatic, bone marrow, or other nodal involvement; no low-grade follicular component is seen, and there is no evidence of double-hit/triple-hit lymphoma. EBER is negative.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage IA, non-bulky, with no B symptoms. FDG PET-CT shows a single nodal region (contiguous right cervical levels II-III), with the largest node 3.1 cm. IPI 0 (age <60, stage I, ECOG 0, normal LDH, no extranodal sites), age-adjusted IPI 0, and CNS-IPI 0.
answer.biology: GCB immunophenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD20+, PAX5+, CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1/IRF4 negative, CD5 negative, cyclin D1 negative, CD30 negative). BCL2 is positive in about 30% and MYC in about 15% of tumor cells, so this is not a double-expressor lymphoma; Ki-67 is about 55% and EBER ISH is negative. FISH shows no MYC, BCL2, or BCL6 rearrangement, excluding double-hit/triple-hit disease. The biology is favorable, although the GCB assignment is based on immunohistochemistry rather than gene-expression profiling.
answer.prognosis: Favorable. Stage IA, non-bulky, GCB, IPI/age-adjusted IPI 0, CNS-IPI 0, non-double-hit, non-double-expressor, and ECOG 0. With R-CHOP-based therapy the expected 5-year progression-free and overall survival exceed 90% (on the order of 95%), and cure is the goal. The main uncertainties are that the GCB subtype is IHC-defined rather than gene-expression-defined, and that the largest/most FDG-avid node was not the node excised; the diagnostic node is nonetheless adequate and the findings are concordant.
answer.first_line_treatment: Curative-intent R-CHOP-21 for 6 cycles without consolidative radiation. R-CHOP is rituximab 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, and vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 (capped at 2 mg) on day 1, with prednisone 100 mg daily on days 1-5, repeated every 21 days. The key reason for choosing chemotherapy alone is that she has favorable limited-stage (IA, non-bulky) GCB DLBCL and strongly wishes to avoid neck radiation because of her sister's radiation-related hypothyroidism and her concerns about thyroid, salivary, and taste toxicity. Six cycles of R-CHOP alone is a NCCN-recognized option for limited-stage DLBCL and was non-inferior to 4 cycles of R-CHOP plus involved-site radiation in the FLYER trial in young, low-risk, non-bulky stage I-II patients. I would not use CNS prophylaxis, and I would not use Pola-R-CHP or other novel regimens, which are not established for stage I disease. If she later changes her priority to the shortest possible chemotherapy course, 4 cycles of R-CHOP followed by 30-36 Gy involved-site radiation would be the alternative; if end-of-treatment PET shows residual disease, I would biopsy it and treat as refractory disease rather than simply adding radiation.
answer.cns_risk: Low. CNS-IPI is 0 (age <60, stage I, ECOG 0, normal LDH, no extranodal sites, no renal/adrenal involvement), corresponding to a very low risk of CNS relapse (well under 1%). I will not give intrathecal methotrexate or high-dose methotrexate CNS prophylaxis, and I will not perform a routine lumbar puncture or brain MRI in the absence of neurologic symptoms. Her migraine with aura is typical and is not evidence of CNS lymphoma; if she develops new focal deficits, a persistent headache different from her usual migraine, cranial neuropathy, or confusion, I will obtain MRI brain with contrast and CSF analysis. I will also stop her combined oral contraceptive during chemotherapy because migraine with aura plus estrogen increases ischemic stroke risk.
answer.response_assessment: Interim PET after 2 cycles is not recommended outside a clinical trial. I will restage with FDG PET-CT from skull base to mid-thigh 6-8 weeks after cycle 6 and interpret it with the Lugano/Deauville 5-point scale. Deauville 1-3 (complete metabolic response) means no further therapy and observation. Deauville 4-5 requires biopsy of the residual site if feasible; if residual DLBCL is confirmed, I will treat as refractory/relapsed disease with second-line platinum-based chemotherapy (for example R-ICE or R-DHAP) and consider autologous stem-cell transplant if chemosensitive, reserving involved-site radiation for localized residual disease not amenable to systemic salvage. After a complete response, follow-up will be history and examination every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months, without routine surveillance imaging; I will monitor blood counts, cardiac function, ovarian function/fertility, and age-appropriate cancer screening.
answer.pretreatment_workup: Already completed and adequate: excisional right cervical node biopsy with immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, and FISH; FDG PET-CT; CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, and uric acid; HIV, hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs), and hepatitis C serologies; and baseline echocardiogram (LVEF 63%). Before starting R-CHOP I will add: a serum beta-hCG to exclude pregnancy, since she is premenopausal and on an oral contraceptive; urgent reproductive-endocrinology referral with AMH/antral follicle count and oocyte or embryo cryopreservation (a 2-4 week delay is acceptable for stage IA non-bulky disease), plus discussion of a GnRH agonist during chemotherapy; baseline TSH given the family history of thyroid disease and the possibility that neck radiation could later be needed; a documented baseline neurologic/neuropathy assessment for vincristine; review and update of inactivated vaccines (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal) before chemotherapy, with live vaccines avoided; and a contraception plan that stops the combined oral contraceptive in favor of a progestin-only or non-hormonal method. Bone marrow biopsy and lumbar puncture are not indicated because PET shows no marrow or CNS involvement. No hepatitis B antiviral prophylaxis is needed because she is anti-HBc negative and anti-HBs positive (immune).
answer.supportive_care: I will use pegfilgrastim 6 mg subcutaneously on day 2 for primary febrile-neutropenia prophylaxis, which also helps preserve dose intensity and her teaching schedule. Antiemetic prophylaxis will be a 5-HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone, with olanzapine or an NK1 antagonist added if control is inadequate; codeine will be avoided because of her allergy. I will add a bowel regimen for vincristine/ondansetron-related constipation. Tumor-lysis risk is low (stage I, normal LDH, low bulk), so I will use oral hydration and monitor uric acid, potassium, phosphorus, calcium, and creatinine, without rasburicase; allopurinol is not routinely needed. No PJP prophylaxis is required for 5-day prednisone pulses, and no HBV antiviral prophylaxis is needed given her immune serology. She should stop the combined oral contraceptive and use a progestin-only or non-hormonal method; I will not use routine anticoagulation, but I will maintain mobility and have a low threshold to evaluate VTE. I will monitor for vincristine neuropathy and dose-modify for grade 2 or higher toxicity. Cardiac function will be monitored given doxorubicin (cumulative 300 mg/m2), with a repeat echocardiogram if symptoms develop or at completion. She may continue sumatriptan for migraines as needed, but should avoid codeine. I will encourage exercise, nutrition, oral/dental hygiene, and prompt evaluation of fever; inactivated vaccines are appropriate, but live vaccines are contraindicated during therapy. I will also address fertility preservation and ovarian-function monitoring, provide psychosocial support, and arrange work accommodations such as treating on Friday and returning to teaching on Monday.
answer.fitness_and_goals: Very fit: a 45-year-old woman with ECOG 0, weight 64 kg, BSA 1.72 m2, normal CBC/CMP, normal LDH, LVEF 63%, no cardiac or pulmonary disease, never smoker, and working full time. She is a candidate for full-dose curative R-CHOP. Her goals are cure, preservation of fertility, and maintaining her teaching schedule, and she wants to avoid neck radiation. I will prioritize fertility preservation before starting chemotherapy, choose an RT-free regimen (6 cycles of R-CHOP), schedule treatment to minimize missed work, and explicitly document that the goal is curative. At age 45 her ovarian reserve is likely reduced, and cyclophosphamide carries a meaningful risk of premature ovarian insufficiency, so fertility counseling should not delay treatment beyond a few weeks. If she develops significant toxicity or her goals change, we will reassess; at present there is no role for reduced-intensity or palliative therapy.
missing_information: No serum beta-hCG pregnancy test is in the record; a negative result must be documented before starting rituximab/cyclophosphamide.
No ovarian reserve assessment (AMH, antral follicle count) or documented fertility-preservation counseling/decision; she is undecided about another pregnancy.
No explicit Ann Arbor stage, IPI, or CNS-IPI is documented in the chart, although all can be derived from the available data (stage IA, IPI 0, CNS-IPI 0).
No baseline TSH/thyroid function is documented, which is relevant given her sister's radiation-related hypothyroidism and the possibility that neck radiation could become necessary.
No formal baseline neurologic/neuropathy assessment for vincristine is documented; the exam is non-focal but does not substitute for a dedicated baseline.
No vaccination history/status (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal) or documented plan to update inactivated vaccines before chemotherapy is available.
No documented contraception plan during chemotherapy or discussion of discontinuing the combined oral contraceptive.

The largest and most FDG-avid node (right level IIA, 3.1 cm, SUVmax 14.2) was not excised; the diagnostic biopsy was from the level III node. This is adequate for diagnosis, but re-biopsy of the residual level IIA node would be needed if the response is discordant or transformation is suspected.

No gene-expression profiling (for example Lymph2Cx) or TP53/molecular profiling is available; GCB assignment rests on Hans immunohistochemistry, which is about 80% concordant with gene-expression profiling. This is not required for standard treatment but is a source of uncertainty.

No dedicated contrast-enhanced diagnostic CT is available (only the low-dose CT from PET-CT); this would be needed for precise measurements and radiation planning if involved-site radiation were later required.
No baseline dental evaluation is documented; this is optional before chemotherapy but would be reasonable if time permits.

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage I (stage IA acceptable): a single nodal region (right cervical levels II-III).
The response notes the disease is non-bulky (largest node 3.1 cm, below 7.5 cm) and that there are no B symptoms.
The response notes that bone marrow biopsy is unnecessary because PET-CT shows no marrow uptake.
The response overstages the disease as stage III or IV / advanced stage.
The response states the lymphoma is neither double-expressor (MYC 15%, BCL2 30% below thresholds) nor double-hit (FISH negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-expressor.
The response calculates IPI as 0 (low risk): age <=60, normal LDH, ECOG 0, stage I, no extranodal sites.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 0 / low risk.
The response recommends curative-intent rituximab-containing immunochemotherapy (R-CHOP-based) for this patient.

The response recommends, as the preferred plan, 4 cycles of R-CHOP followed by 2 additional doses of rituximab without radiotherapy (FLYER regimen; age 18-60, IPI 0, non-bulky <7.5 cm). A 4-cycle PET-adapted R-CHOP approach is also accepted.
The response notes that the chosen plan omits neck radiotherapy, which aligns with her wish to avoid radiation (thyroid and salivary late effects, sister's radiation-induced hypothyroidism).
The response names R-CHOP x3 followed by involved-site radiotherapy, or a PET-adapted 4-cycle approach (S1001), as an acceptable alternative.
The response recommends 6 cycles of R-CHOP (or of Pola-R-CHP) as the preferred plan for this IPI-0, non-bulky stage I disease (overtreatment).
The response recommends Pola-R-CHP as the preferred regimen (POLARIX enrolled IPI 2-5 only; not indicated at IPI 0).
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R or another intensified regimen for this patient.
The response recommends observation / no systemic treatment, or radiotherapy alone, as the plan.
The response judges CNS-relapse risk as low and states that CNS prophylaxis and CNS staging (MRI brain / lumbar puncture) are not indicated.
The response recommends CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal chemotherapy or high-dose methotrexate) for this patient.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.

The response plans an interim PET-CT after cycle 4 (before the rituximab-only doses) and says a positive scan (Deauville 4-5) would prompt additional therapy (e.g. RT or biopsy) rather than proceeding as planned.
The response requires a pregnancy test (serum or urine hCG) before starting chemotherapy, noting that none is documented in this premenopausal woman.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) so no antiviral prophylaxis is needed before rituximab.
The response notes the baseline LVEF of 63% permits anthracycline.

The response stops the combined estrogen-containing oral contraceptive and switches to effective non-estrogen contraception (e.g. copper or levonorgestrel IUD, implant, progestin-only method) for the duration of treatment.

The response gives the reason: estrogen-containing contraception is contraindicated in migraine with aura (ischemic stroke risk) and adds venous thromboembolism risk during chemotherapy/active cancer.
The response offers fertility / ovarian-function counselling (abbreviated R-CHOP has low gonadotoxicity; referral to reproductive medicine offered since she is undecided about further pregnancy).
The response judges her fit (ECOG 0, no limiting comorbidity) for curative-intent therapy with a high cure probability, and addresses her goals of continuing to work and avoiding neck radiation.
